title: Salford firebomb killer released by police despite 'last chance' warning

evidence_packet.title: Salford firebomb killer released by police despite 'last chance' warning

evidence_packet.summary: Zak Bolland was released 13 days before he murdered a woman and four children in a firebomb attack
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford firebomb killer released by police despite 'last chance' warning - BBC News Image source, Family photos Image caption, The four Pearson children died during the petrol bomb attack, and their mother died 20 months later Published 6 October 2026 A man who murdered a mother and her four children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police a fortnight before, despite a judge having told him he was on his "last chance", an inquest has heard. Zak Bolland, then 23, left a police station after giving a 12-minute "no comment" interview for breaking windows at the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Walkden, Salford, Greater Manchester, on 26 November 2017. Bolland's record was not checked at the time and he was told no further action would be taken, Bolton Coroner's Court heard. Thirteen days later he petrol bombed the house, killing the children and severely burning their mother, who died 20 months later. Demi, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and seven-year-old sister Lacie, who were sleeping in a front bedroom, all died in the blaze. Michelle suffered 68% burns to her body and "clung on to life" until she died on 25 August 2019. On the second day of an eight-week inquest, police who had been involved with the family before the fatal attack were questioned. PC John Worthington of Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told the inquest he went to the house after the windows were smashed and Bolland was named as the culprit. Finance bosses at Bury Council have said rising costs and dwindling reserves mean they are not able to balance the books without intervention, and there could be a three-year budget gap of £35m. Even with savings identified, that gap is expected to come to £9.6m for the coming financial year, and rising to £17.5m at the end of three years. The council said the decisions it was making, and "even the ones we haven't made yet" were all "regrettable". Town halls are legally bound to present a balanced budget each year or they must file a Section 114 notice, which would effectively declare them bankrupt, so Bury Council is seeking solutions to avoid that eventuality/ It has become the second Greater Manchester authority to apply for Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) in recent years, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. 'Won't be enough' Trafford Council is the other, and two years into receiving EFS, residents have seen council tax increases of 7.49% each year. Finance leaders at Bury have stated they do not believe borrowing was the solution for the council, but did not rule out tax rises of more than 4.99% if the government allowed it. Best known as Eileen Grimshaw in ITV soap Coronation Street, Cleaver is among the famous faces joining the new production, which is the first to be commissioned by Wood's estate since her death in 2016 at the age of 62. The 63-year-old, who featured in the BBC show as a recurring character, will take the stage as cynical canteen worker Jean, who was played by Anne Reid in the show. She said the script it "blew her away" and that it had been "beautifully adapted" from Wood's show. The show, created, written and co-produced by Wood, aired on the BBC from 1998 to 2000 and followed the workplace dramas of the staff and regulars in a canteen at a factory in Manchester. More than 25 years on, Cleaver told BBC Radio Manchester the sitcom, which ran for two series was "observational comedy at its finest". She said: "I'm thrilled to be doing it. "It's such a celebration of Vic's work. It's about the celebration of her and her legacy. "I think she'd be over the moon and I'm very excited to be a part of it." Cleaver added: "There's no way [the audience] are not going to be able to enjoy this show. "It's a British classic and nobody writes the way Vic writes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who murdered a mother and her four children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police a fortnight before, despite a judge having told him he was on his "last chance", an inquest has heard Zak Bolland, then 23, left a police station after giving a 12-minute "no comment" interview for breaking windows at the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Walkden, Salford, Greater Manchester, on 26 November 2017 Bolland's record was not checked at the time and he was told no further action would be taken, Bolton Coroner's Court heard Thirteen days later he petrol bombed the house, killing the children and severely burning their mother, who died 20 months later Demi, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and seven-year-old sister Lacie, who were sleeping in a front bedroom, all died in the blaze Michelle suffered 68% burns to her body and "clung on to life" until she died on 25 August 2019

title: Bury Council seeking government cash support to plug £9.6m deficit

evidence_packet.title: Bury Council seeking government cash support to plug £9.6m deficit
evidence_packet.lead: People living in part of Greater Manchester could face service cuts and tax increases after a council revealed it is seeking emergency financial aid from the government Finance bosses at Bury Council have said rising costs and dwindling reserves mean they are not able to balance
evidence_packet.summary: People living in part of Greater Manchester could face service cuts and tax increases after a council revealed it is seeking emergency financial aid from the government Finance bosses at Bury Council have said rising costs and dwindling reserves mean they are not able to balance
evidence_packet.evidence_text: People living in part of Greater Manchester could face service cuts and tax increases after a council revealed it is seeking emergency financial aid from the government Finance bosses at Bury Council have said rising costs and dwindling reserves mean they are not able to balance the books without intervention, and there could be a three-year budget gap of £35m Even with savings identified, that gap is expected to come to £9.6m for the coming financial year, and rising to £17.5m at the end of three years The council said the decisions it was making, and "even the ones we haven't made yet" were all "regrettable" Town halls are legally bound to present a balanced budget each year or they must file a Section 114 notice, which would effectively declare them bankrupt, so Bury Council is seeking solutions to avoid that eventuality/ It has become the second Greater Manchester authority to apply for Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) in recent years, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said

Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local De The battle to win a key seat in a ‘forgotten’ Greater Manchester town is on as Labour and Reform prepare to battle it out A date has now been set for the upcoming by-election in Failsworth West, a ward in Oldham . The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health On September 24, Coun Wilkinson said he would be stepping down as both leader of the borough’s 16-strong Reform UK group, as well as an elected member for Failsworth, for health reasons. This was just days after he was elected replacing Lewis Quigg Coun Wilkinson said he had been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and atrial fibrillation following a visit to Royal Oldham Hospital, adding: “This has inevitably made me take a serious look at my health and my future “I have been advised by medical professionals to take things easy and get plenty of rest.”

The new unit, called Birch 100, will be built in the south east corner of the 15.6 hectare estate It is expected to play a part in boosting the industrial and logistics operations already in operation, situated next to junction 3 of the M66 and junction 19 of the M62 The land was previously used for storage of portacabins, cranes and other construction site equipment. The tenants for the new site, McCarthy and Stone, are expected to use the new facility for maintenance of HGVs and cranes as well as a fuelling point The scheme is being delivered by urban logistics developer and investment manager, Chancerygate, who will also refurbish three other units on the estate. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Hospital Cheshire dad, 39, told he had two years to live after discovering 'widow-maker' Ellis Dawson suffered a severe blockage in an artery known as the "widow-maker" Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inn A 39-year-old dad who suffered a heart attack while playing football has told of how he was later given just two years to live Ellis Dawson, from Mow Cop, Cheshire, began to feel "funny" during a game - a symptom that eventually led to him being told by doctors he had just two years left to live The "fit and healthy" dad-of-two underwent a heart transplant in February this year after a severe blockage in an artery known as the "widow-maker" Just months after his transplant at Wythenshawe Hospital, Ellis says he is feeling "incredibly positive" about the future He said: "It is impossible to express the depth of gratitude I feel towards my donor's family for giving me the ultimate gift: the chance to watch my two little girls grow up. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Buses Rochdale's £2.50 bus ride is the best thing to cross the Pennines since Eric Cantona From the top deck of the 590 you can take a trip through Greater Manchester's rich industrial heritage while taking in some of the the region's most dramatic sc And to that list you can add the 590 bus . The Rochdale to Halifax service swaps the Roch Valley for the Calder Valley as it crosses over from Greater Manchester into West Yorkshire And along the way it takes in two marvels of the Industrial Revolution and plenty of the region's most dramatic scenery. I caught the 590 this week as far as Hebden Bridge as part of our occasional series on Greater Manchester's most scenic bus routes The first thing to note is because this is a privately-owned First Bus and not a publicly-controlled Bee Network service a single ticket is £2.50 not two quid. Having stumped up the extra 10 bob, I head upstairs to join a handful of students heading home after lectures on the top From Rochdale bus station it heads east out of the town centre through Smallbridge and Littleborough before crossing the border at Summit into the towns of Walsden, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Changes planned to street trading rules in Manchester includes steps against 'nuisance' operators A consultation has been launched. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:57, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Image New changes to street trading rules in Manchester are being planned with measures to crackdown on ‘nuisance or disturbance’ from traders in the city Manchester council has launched a consultation on its plans which aim to make the rules ‘simpler and more up to date’ and ‘help manage public spaces more effectively’ The draft policy has been published on the council website while the consultation runs to November. The town hall said it would give it more control over where street trading takes place and help to spot unsuitable locations earlier It includes a section about nuisances around noise levels and smells from street trading. The document reads: “Applications will be assessed for their potential impact on nearby residents and sensitive premises such as schools, hospitals, and places of worship “There will be a presumption against trading from taking place at or immediately adjacent to a residential property. This is to prevent nuisance or disturbance to residents caused by commercial activities.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: HMRC HMRC hits 11 Greater Manchester firms with £3.3m in fines as it names and shames businesses Those named by the government department include a taxi driver, a clothes retailer and three takeaways View 2 Images Eleven firms across Greater Mancheste Add to preferred sources Comments News Elliot Jessett and Charlotte Fisher Reporter 17:14, 06 Oct 2026 A total of 11 firms across Greater Manchester have been named and shamed by HMRC for failing to pay their taxes in full. HMRC published a list of more than 130 people and busine HMRC has issued penalties in each case for each of the entities named on the list - totalling more than £3,300,000 charged to the Greater Manchester firms in total The entities across Greater Manchester include a tax repayment agent, a taxi driver, a stairlift and disability bathrooms supplier and three takeaways The list covers civil penalties only and does not include criminal convictions for tax fraud, and the details remain published for 12 months. The cases relate to businesses which did not pay at least £25,000 in tax, or make a full disclosure when HMRC began its investigation – a The information is only released once the penalties are final. The list below includes those individuals and companies who had an address in Greater Manchester at the time of the default, alongside the nature of their business, the period of default and the fines they were given

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Firebomb killer was released by police after threatening to torch Michelle Pearson's home and smashing windows weeks before deadly arson attack, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and her four children following a devas Add to preferred sources News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 17:03, 06 Oct 2026 Murderer Zak Bolland was arrested after smashing windows at Michelle Pearson's home - and threatening to petrol bomb the property - weeks before he launched the arson attack that claimed the lives of th He walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute 'no comment' interview having targeted the home of Michelle, 37, and her young family on Jackson Street in Walkden , Greater Manchester on November 26, 2017 An inquest into the deaths of the mother and her children has heard Bolland was released with no further action being taken, despite being on a suspended sentence for other crimes - and having recently been given a 'last chance' by a judge Bolland, Bolton Coroners' Court heard, chillingly told Michelle in texts: " I want £500, or I will finish your house off. I am going to petrol bomb your house tonight." The firebombing on Jackson Street in Walkden, Salford, in December 2017 claimed the lives of Michelle and her children - Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven, and Lia, three

It comes after City were found guilty of more than 100 charges Manchester City was found guilty last week of charges relating to alleged breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons According to the Premier League, an independent commission concluded that the club had arranged “sham” commercial agreements with several sponsors during the period The commission found that the arrangements formed part of a disguised funding scheme, under which the companies involved paid only part of the relevant sponsorship fees It concluded that the remaining money was provided by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, which was the club's majority owner

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat Mario-Vifor Ratoiu and Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu are due to be sentenced in December Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:06, 06 Oct 2 Two men have admitted sexual
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat Mario-Vifor Ratoiu and Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu are due to be sentenced in December Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:06, 06 Oct 2 Two men have admitted sexual offences after a teenage girl was raped in a flat in Manchester city centre Mario-Vifor Ratoiu, 23, admitted raping the 14-year-old. Co-defendant Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu, 26, pleaded guilty to engaging in sexual activity with a child, having previously been charged with rape Prosecutors told Manchester Crown Court Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu's plea to the less serious charge was acceptable. Both men, of no fixed address, are due to be sentenced at the same court in December The charges came after police received a report of a rape at a flat in the Green Quarter area of the city in April. The defendants, both Romanian nationals, were arrested and remanded in custody, where they remain The full circumstances of the case have not yet been outlined in open court. They entered guilty pleas ahead of a proposed trial, which was due to start today (October 6)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: National news Police issue new update amid 'speculation' after body of girl, 11, found in UK park Miya Deamer-Jones was tragically found dead in a park near a cricket club in Elmley Castle in Worcestershire Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Police have issued an investigation update while urging people not to speculate after an 11-year-old girl was tragically found dead in a park in Worcestershire. Miya Deamer-Jones was first reported missing at around 11.20pm on Sunday (October 4) Sadly, her body was later found in the park near the cricket ground in Elmley Castle, West Mercia Police said. Police launched an investigation with detectives treating her death as 'unexplained' Today (October 6) detectives said they are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding Miya's death. Police said they are 'not trying to identify any third party involved' as they urged people not to speculate In a statement, West Mercia Police said: "Detectives continue to investigate the death of an 11-year-old girl in Elmley Castle, near Pershore. The girl was reported missing at around 11.20pm on Sunday 4 October and was later sadly found deceased in the park near the cricket groun "Her death is currently being treated as unexplained while officers work to establish the circumstances surrounding what happened. Her family continue to be supported by specially trained officers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform and Labour prepare to battle for key seat in 'forgotten' town The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health. Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local De The battle to win a key seat in a ‘forgotten’ Greater Manchester town is on as Labour and Reform prepare to battle it out A date has now been set for the upcoming by-election in Failsworth West, a ward in Oldham . The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health On September 24, Coun Wilkinson said he would be stepping down as both leader of the borough’s 16-strong Reform UK group, as well as an elected member for Failsworth, for health reasons. This was just days after he was elected replacing Lewis Quigg Coun Wilkinson said he had been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and atrial fibrillation following a visit to Royal Oldham Hospital, adding: “This has inevitably made me take a serious look at my health and my future “I have been advised by medical professionals to take things easy and get plenty of rest.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury 'Regrettable decisions' loom as Bury residents face service cuts and huge tax rises Bury council said it will be seeking emergency financial support from the Government for the coming year Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson Residents face service cuts and huge tax rises as Bury council seeks emergency financial aid from the government With dwindling reserves and ever-mounting costs, finance bosses at the council say they do not believe they can set a legal budget for the coming years without Exceptional Financial Support (EFS). If nothing changes, leaders predict their three-budget gap could hit £35m Even with identified savings, that gap would still be £9.6m for the coming financial year 2027/28, rising to £17.5m at the end of three years. Town halls are legally bound to present a balanced budget each year or must file a Section 114 notice, effectively declaring themselves b This announcement makes Bury council the second Greater Manchester authority to apply for EFS in recent years, with Trafford council currently in its second year of emergency aid . For Trafford residents, this has resulted in two years of huge council tax rises with increases at Finance leads at Bury council sat down with the Manchester Evening News to set out the authority’s position. They said they did not believe borrowing was the solution for the council, but did not rule out tax rises of more than 4.99pc if the Government allowed it

Tony Steenson's passion for the game was legendary, as was his ability to drill a solid defence. But he was also known for his knack of organising numerous charity games in w Tributes are now pouring in for Tony who sadly died aged 78 last week after taking ill on holiday in Portugal. He counted scores of sports stars and celebrities as friends Tony famously organised the All Stars charity football matches raising hundreds of thousands of pounds for charity over the past 50 years in Manchester. He also played for Hyde United, Salford Amateurs, and Mossley As well as his skill, his non-stop talking on and off the pitch and red-hair made him a well-known and respected character. Tony worked as sales director for Newsquest Media during his professional life, while in his personal life he organised hundreds of events for charity with Coronation Street star Alan Halsall was among a host of stars paying tribute to Tony, sharing a photo with "The Gaffa" caption, he posted the emotional message: "I love you mate. Phase one of the scheme will focus on Bradshawgate and Great Moor Street Roads will be resurfaced and footpaths repaved to make them more attractive and benefit people travelling on foot. There will be changes at side roads to give pedestrians priority, along with an upgraded pedestrian crossing on Bradshawgate, near Nelson Square Four junctions will be upgraded to make it easier and safer for people on foot and riding bikes to travel around the town centre. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Buses Rochdale's £2.50 bus ride is the best thing to cross the Pennines since Eric Cantona From the top deck of the 590 you can take a trip through Greater Manchester's rich industrial heritage while taking in some of the the region's most dramatic sc And to that list you can add the 590 bus . The Rochdale to Halifax service swaps the Roch Valley for the Calder Valley as it crosses over from Greater Manchester into West Yorkshire And along the way it takes in two marvels of the Industrial Revolution and plenty of the region's most dramatic scenery. I caught the 590 this week as far as Hebden Bridge as part of our occasional series on Greater Manchester's most scenic bus routes The first thing to note is because this is a privately-owned First Bus and not a publicly-controlled Bee Network service a single ticket is £2.50 not two quid. Having stumped up the extra 10 bob, I head upstairs to join a handful of students heading home after lectures on the top From Rochdale bus station it heads east out of the town centre through Smallbridge and Littleborough before crossing the border at Summit into the towns of Walsden, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Changes planned to street trading rules in Manchester includes steps against 'nuisance' operators A consultation has been launched. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:57, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Image New changes to street trading rules in Manchester are being planned with measures to crackdown on ‘nuisance or disturbance’ from traders in the city Manchester council has launched a consultation on its plans which aim to make the rules ‘simpler and more up to date’ and ‘help manage public spaces more effectively’ The draft policy has been published on the council website while the consultation runs to November. The town hall said it would give it more control over where street trading takes place and help to spot unsuitable locations earlier It includes a section about nuisances around noise levels and smells from street trading. The document reads: “Applications will be assessed for their potential impact on nearby residents and sensitive premises such as schools, hospitals, and places of worship “There will be a presumption against trading from taking place at or immediately adjacent to a residential property. This is to prevent nuisance or disturbance to residents caused by commercial activities.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Prison visitor gave 'illogical' explanation after staff noticed he was wearing two pairs of trousers Rhys Carter had attended HMP Forest Bank in Salford Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:02, 06 Oct 2026 Vi A would-be drug smuggler was caught out after prison security staff noticed he was wearing two pairs of trousers Rhys Carter, 35, went to HMP Forest Bank in Salford with a woman visiting a relative. He was found with cannabis, tobacco and an iPhone, all prohibited items within the jail which had been secreted on his person At one point when he was questioned Carter tried to leave, and ran away barefoot. When he was caught and questioned by police, Carter gave an 'illogical' explanation, Manchester Crown Court heard Prosecuting, Ellie-Louise Fradley said Carter attended the prison on September 24, 2024, with an unnamed woman. The woman was due to visit a relative of hers Carter was asked to enter a search booth on entry to the prison, and replied 'no' when asked if he had anything on him which he shouldn't have. He had aroused the suspicion of prison staff 'due to the fact he was wearing two pairs of trousers', Ms Fradley said

HMRC published a list of more than 130 people and busine HMRC has issued penalties in each case for each of the entities named on the list - totalling more than £3,300,000 charged to the Greater Manchester firms in total The entities across Greater Manchester include a tax repayment agent, a taxi driver, a stairlift and disability bathrooms supplier and three takeaways The list covers civil penalties only and does not include criminal convictions for tax fraud, and the details remain published for 12 months. The cases relate to businesses which did not pay at least £25,000 in tax, or make a full disclosure when HMRC began its investigation – a The information is only released once the penalties are final. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City FC Kemi Badenoch challenges Andy Burnham to publish 'everything' linked to Man City dealings Kemi Badenoch has called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham to publish all dealings with Manchester City Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Kemi Badenoch has called on Andy Burnham to publish “everything” relating to his dealings with Manchester City, after the Prime Minister intervened to defend the football club's owners. It comes after City were found guilty of more than 100 charges Manchester City was found guilty last week of charges relating to alleged breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons According to the Premier League, an independent commission concluded that the club had arranged “sham” commercial agreements with several sponsors during the period The commission found that the arrangements formed part of a disguised funding scheme, under which the companies involved paid only part of the relevant sponsorship fees It concluded that the remaining money was provided by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, which was the club's majority owner

title: Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat

evidence_packet.title: Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat Mario-Vifor Ratoiu and Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu are due to be sentenced in December Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:06, 06 Oct 2 Two men have admitted sexual
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat Mario-Vifor Ratoiu and Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu are due to be sentenced in December Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:06, 06 Oct 2 Two men have admitted sexual
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Two men admit sexual offences after teenage girl raped at Manchester city centre flat Mario-Vifor Ratoiu and Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu are due to be sentenced in December Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:06, 06 Oct 2 Two men have admitted sexual offences after a teenage girl was raped in a flat in Manchester city centre Mario-Vifor Ratoiu, 23, admitted raping the 14-year-old. Co-defendant Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu, 26, pleaded guilty to engaging in sexual activity with a child, having previously been charged with rape Prosecutors told Manchester Crown Court Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu's plea to the less serious charge was acceptable. Both men, of no fixed address, are due to be sentenced at the same court in December The charges came after police received a report of a rape at a flat in the Green Quarter area of the city in April. The defendants, both Romanian nationals, were arrested and remanded in custody, where they remain The full circumstances of the case have not yet been outlined in open court. They entered guilty pleas ahead of a proposed trial, which was due to start today (October 6)

evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Oldham Reform and Labour prepare to battle for key seat in 'forgotten' town The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health. Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local De The battle to win a key seat
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform and Labour prepare to battle for key seat in 'forgotten' town The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health. Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local De The battle to win a key seat in a ‘forgotten’ Greater Manchester town is on as Labour and Reform prepare to battle it out A date has now been set for the upcoming by-election in Failsworth West, a ward in Oldham . The seat was previously held by former Reform UK leader Mark Wilkinson who stepped down due to ill health On September 24, Coun Wilkinson said he would be stepping down as both leader of the borough’s 16-strong Reform UK group, as well as an elected member for Failsworth, for health reasons. This was just days after he was elected replacing Lewis Quigg Coun Wilkinson said he had been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and atrial fibrillation following a visit to Royal Oldham Hospital, adding: “This has inevitably made me take a serious look at my health and my future “I have been advised by medical professionals to take things easy and get plenty of rest.”

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.summary: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Best known as Eileen Grimshaw in ITV soap Coronation Street, Cleaver is among the famous faces joining the new production, which is the first to be commissioned by Wood's estate since her death in 2016 at the age of 62 The 63-year-old, who featured in the BBC show as a recurring character, will take the stage as cynical canteen worker Jean, who was played by Anne Reid in the show She said the script it "blew her away" and that it had been "beautifully adapted" from Wood's show The show, created, written and co-produced by Wood, aired on the BBC from 1998 to 2000 and followed the workplace dramas of the staff and regulars in a canteen at a factory in Manchester More than 25 years on, Cleaver told BBC Radio Manchester the sitcom, which ran for two series was "observational comedy at its finest" "It's such a celebration of Vic's work. It's about the celebration of her and her legacy

Thousands of visitors from across Oldham and beyond flocked to the site to experience Oldham’s newest major visitor attraction. They could explore Snipe Clough Farm, a new four-acre working urban farm, and make wildflower seed bombs with the friendly team of volunteers. evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements. These measures are designed to strengthen democratic oversight, provide clear political leadership across key service areas and support transparent decision-making while the borough continues to work towards the appointment of a Council Leader and Cabinet. The arrangements were approved by Council on 16 September and include the creation of interim Lead Member and Deputy Lead Member roles aligned to the Council's four directorates. The arrangements form part of a wider governance framework developed following legal advice, engagement with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and discussions between political group leaders. Under the arrangements, Chief Executive Shelley Kipling will continue to exercise delegated executive powers, while Lead Members provide political oversight, advocacy and a visible link between residents, councillors and services. The roles carry no executive decision-making powers. The four Interim Lead Member portfolios have been allocated to the Council's four largest political groups, with deputy roles assigned from the same groups. Interim Lead Member appointments Resources - Lead Member: Sam Al-Hamdani (Liberal Democrats) - Deputy Lead Member: Mark Kenyon (Liberal Democrats) The Resources portfolio will provide political oversight of the Council's finances, budget management, transformation programme, corporate services, governance, workforce and organisational performance. Place - Lead Member: Arooj Shah (Labour) - Deputy Lead Member: Elaine Taylor (Labour) The Place portfolio will focus on regeneration, economic growth, planning, housing, highways, environmental services, transport and the continued delivery of major projects that support Oldham

title: Council secures court order following unauthorised encampment at Oldham Edge

evidence_packet.title: Council secures court order following unauthorised encampment at Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge. Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August. As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their vehicles and belongings. The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime. After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment. The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team. A Council spokesperson said: “We understand the concerns raised by residents and people using Oldham Edge, and we thank them for their patience while we followed the legal process. “We always try to resolve unauthorised encampments through discussion and voluntary cooperation wherever possible. However, when the site was not vacated as agreed, it became necessary to take further action. “We worked closely with Greater Manchester Police throughout to make sure the situation was handled lawfully and proportionately. “The encampment has now left and our cleansing team has completed the clean-up, allowing the area to be returned to the local community.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture. Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up. Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding. Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year. A huge Oldham welcome to: Sew Oldham – Isobel Pickup and Fay Buchanan The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery. Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home. A New Mural for Oldham – Deggy Art Deggy taught himself how to spray-paint during lockdown, starting with a painting of Joe Exotic. It snowballed from there and his murals can now be seen across Greater Manchester and Derbyshire. He will create a new mural on Oldham’s high street; the subject is a secret for now. We can’t wait to see it! title: Rogue roofer sentenced after targeting and defrauding vulnerable residents

evidence_packet.summary: A rogue trader who targeted vulnerable residents and carried out unnecessary and substandard roofing work has been sentenced to more than five years in prison following a prosecution brought by Wigan Council's Trading Standards team At a hearing at Bolton Crown Court on Wednesday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A rogue trader who targeted vulnerable residents and carried out unnecessary and substandard roofing work has been sentenced to more than five years in prison following a prosecution brought by Wigan Council's Trading Standards team At a hearing at Bolton Crown Court on Wednesday 2th September, Tyrone Young, the owner of ACL Roofing and Staydry, was sentenced in his absence to a total of 5 years and 4 months in prison after pleading guilty to fraud and trading regulatory offences, with a warrant outstanding At the sentencing hearing, it was explained that Young had previously received a suspended sentence at Burnley Crown Court in December 2022, for offences in which he “coerced people and did unnecessary and inadequate work” Despite this, Young breached the terms of his sentence and was sent to prison. Yet within a month of his release, he committed similar offences in Wigan Borough in September 2023. This involved the business owner “lying about his name, advising work was required when it wasn’t, i In February 2024, the court heard that Young committed offences against a second victim, where he “cold called the victim, lied to them, made false assertions, and was deliberately aggressive and intimidating”, with the completed work also described as “unnecessary and inadequate With the help of Trading Standards officers, the victims read out powerful personal impact statements to the court, explaining how Young’s coercive and unscrupulous behaviour had devastated them. One victim was living with a terminally ill husband and now can’t afford to fix her

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

The fact that you are now reading this text, perhaps buying a ticket (or already have!), and will soon spend an hour in a room full of strangers, not knowing what’s to come – we find that deeply hopeful. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This month, Connie Kerr’s award-winning play Spent Hen comes to 53two this October, bringing a darkly comic and deeply personal exploration of childlessness, its attendant social stigma and the relentlessly complicated expectations placed on women Winner of the OffCut 2025 Judges’ Award for Writing, the new full-length play follows a woman who always assumed she would become a mother, until it simply doesn’t happen. Having ended her marriage the year she turned 40 and begun questioning the life she once imagined for hersel A former features editor at a glossy fashion magazine, she finds work at a local newspaper – and is promptly tasked with interviewing a series of distressingly inspiring women who appear to be effortlessly balancing successful careers with motherhood. Initially, these encounters Inspired by Kerr’s own experiences, Spent Hen gradually moves from isolation towards tentative optimism, as its protagonist begins speaking openly about miscarriage, infertility and childlessness, finding that the stories she has kept to herself resonate far more widely than she As Kerr questions the images of perfect families that can alienate those who cannot or do not have children, the play grows into a candid, wry exploration of grief and identity, while thoughtfully confronting the social pressure to conform to a rigid conception of a fulfilled lif Spent Hen runs at 53two from Wed 21 to Fri 23 October, before heading to Audenshaw’s Guide Bridge Theatre on Wed 28 Oct

evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.summary: Paul Scholes has hit back at pundit Martin Keown after the former Arsenal defender suggested Manchester City's Premier League titles should be voided if the club's financial breaches are upheld
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Paul Scholes furious with Man City punishment claim and tells pundit to 'do one' Paul Scholes has hit back at pundit Martin Keown after the former Arsenal defender suggested Manchester City's Premier League titles should be voided if the club's Paul Scholes has told Martin Keown to "do one" after the former Arsenal defender suggested Manchester City's honours between 2009 and 2018 should be wiped from the record following their guilty verdict The Premier League confirmed last week that City had been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them, with the club accused of using "sham" sponsorship deals to inflate their income by almost £900million over a nine-year period City have strongly denied any wrongdoing and appealed the verdict last Thursday. The club insists it is "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and claims to have "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support its case Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! One argument reportedly being used by City in their appeal is that the additional funding came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG). Such arrangements are permitted under Premier League rules

title: Man City charges appeal dealt fresh blow by 'UEFA evidence' as £30m claim made

evidence_packet.title: Man City charges appeal dealt fresh blow by 'UEFA evidence' as £30m claim made
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City's appeal against their guilty verdict for financial breaches faces a fresh setback
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City's appeal against their guilty verdict for financial breaches faces a fresh setback
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City charges appeal dealt fresh blow by 'UEFA evidence' as £30m claim made Manchester City's appeal against their guilty verdict for financial breaches faces a fresh setback Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Mark Wakefield Sport Central Manchester City have been handed a fresh blow to their hopes of a successful appeal against the guilty verdict for financial breaches. Reports have emerged that evidence provided by City to UEFA in a past case could undermine the club’s attempt to clear their name in the appeal Last week saw City be found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges for financial breaches brought against them by the Premier League . The English top flight have claimed that City arranged “sham” sponsorship deals to inflate their revenues by £900million City are maintaining their innocence and are making it clear that they are denying any wrongdoing, claiming to have “irrefutable evidence” that will help their case An independent three-person commission will now oversee City's appeal, with a ruling anticipated before the end of the year. Central to City's defence is the assertion that the alleged 'sham' deals were entirely legitimate and funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the c Premier League regulations permit state-owned bodies to sponsor clubs, which could potentially absolve City of any wrongdoing and demonstrate that ADUG did not fabricate illegitimate arrangements

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Renowned British vocal ensemble The Tallis Scholars, conducted by Peter Phillips, present one of the greatest masterpieces of the a cappella repertoire: Sergei Rachmaninov’s Vespers . Inspired by ancient Slavonic chant and Russian Orthodox traditions, the work remains a landmark Interwoven with Rachmaninov’s score are three contemplative works by Arvo Pärt — Tribute to Caesar , Da Pacem, Domine and O Holy Father Nicholas . Together they form a moving programme exploring faith, remembrance and the universal longing for peace For more information and tickets click on ‘buy ticket’ Cadogan Hall, 5 Sloane Terrace, London SW1X 9DQ Receive our digest once a week with quality Russian events and articles
